scenario.title: MANCHURIAN OFFENSIVE - 9 AUG 1945
intro.text:
MANCHURIAN OFFENSIVE - 9 AUG 1945

Khabarovsk, Far Eastern Russia

At the Tehran and Yalta Conference, the Soviet Union has promised to enter the Pacific Theater within three months after the end of the war in Europe. So we are going to smash the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo with a powerful operation. Your task is to overcome the border rivers near Khabarovsk and quickly advance westward into the interior!

ORDERS
Capture all VH!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Vienna approaches closed before the Germans could form another belt. The city fell ten days later. The men thought that meant they were nearly home. We need to tell them about the eastward orders.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-victory.text: The pursuit reached Vienna with enough guns to finish the battle. The city fell on 13 April; the orders sending us east arrived before the rubble cooled.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-tactical.text: Vienna fell after a hard pursuit and a harder urban battle. We reached the end of Europe with a force already being measured for another railway journey.
line.reaction-lose.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-lose.text: Our pursuit failed to stop a new defence before Vienna. Other armies finished the city battle. The group is going east now; I'd like the men to hear the reassignment from you.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.callback-choice-a.text: Officers who objected to your civilian lanes before Vienna are now using the traffic plan themselves. I haven't asked them to explain the change. Let them keep using it.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: The guns reached Vienna on the roads you cleared. Pavel still thinks the tanks could have gone farther ahead. He's had the whole railway journey to explain it to me.
line.scene-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-0.text: I've replaced the European sheets. Check the scale before you use these river distances. Some of us haven't worked with this ground since before 1941.
line.scene-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.scene-1.text: The tanks are off the trains; workshops and pontoons are following. Some crews thought Prague was their last stop. I need bridge capacities before I ask them to drive any farther.
line.scene-2.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.scene-2.text: Sergei, why have you brought the Seseña report? Pavel has been asking about bridge capacities all morning. Let him have some credit.
line.decision.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.decision.text: We can force the crossings on the first timetable and pursue before the defence understands the scale of the attack, or build secure bridgeheads that can carry the whole army into the interior.
line.decision.choice.race-beyond-the-riv: Force the crossings at once and send mobile columns west before resistance can organise.
Release a nine-strength T-34/85 detachment with 70 experience and fully refuel the core; priority rail movement costs 120 prestige.
line.decision.choice.build-the-bridgehea: Secure every crossing with engineers, artillery, and supply before releasing the pursuit.
Attach a full-strength 1943 engineer detachment with 70 experience, fully replenish ammunition, and give artillery 15 experience; bridging trains cost 100 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-a-0.text: The first columns carry fuel and bridging stores ahead of everything else. Once across, they do not wait for a European-style front to form around them.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-a-1.text: I'd have taken this order without a question in Spain. Now I want the bridge classes and fuel returns before I go. Can the following columns keep up?
line.choice-a-2.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-2.text: The first column crosses on schedule. Miss two reports and the following guns halt at the river, however far the tanks claim to see.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-b-0.text: Then we prepare the bridgeheads first. Report when roads, guns and ambulances can cross. That's what releases the pursuit.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-b-1.text: Nine years ago I would have called the bridgehead a delay. Build it. When the guns and ambulances are across, give me the road before Volkov finds another river.
line.post-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.post-0.text: Pavel, take the crossing order to the crews. Anna, check the first reports with me. Nikolai, we'll talk about the Spain file when they are across.
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-success.speaker: Anna Sokolova
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-success.text: The leading columns were still moving west when the capitulation came. This time I could reach them by radio and tell you where the guns and fuel were. I've put those reports with the Spain file. Pavel may complain that I've spoiled his best tank story.
epilogue.manchuria-bridgehead-success.te: The last guns and ambulances crossed before we began the pursuit. I kept expecting Sergei to find a reason to hold us longer. He didn't. When the capitulation came, I could still call every column. I'll concede that much to him.
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-defeat.speaker: Sergei Volkov
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-defeat.text: The leading columns got beyond their guns and stopped. Japan has capitulated, so they won't have to renew the attack. We still have to bring the detachments back together. Pavel and I approved those movement times; put both names on the report.
epilogue.manchuria-bridgehead-defeat.tex: The crossings were prepared and the force is intact. We didn't break the border defence before the war ended. I kept asking for one more confirmation. Commander, I need to account for how much time that cost us.
